title: Overnight Safety Runner — Minimal fail-closed batch executor for overnight execution
description: Implement an isolated Python ops runner that wraps a batch of shell commands, enforces per-task timeout, inactivity/heartbeat timeout, global timeout, process-group termination, and structured logging. The runner is a short-term bridge for tonight's batch execution and does NOT replace the Global Session Shutdown Manager. It must NOT call shutdown/poweroff/halt/osascript/pmset or modify canonical Coordinator/Strategist/ProjectRunner/Execution Runtime.
objectives: Create scripts/overnight_runner.py entry point with --config and --dry-run CLI flags
Create scripts/overnight_runner/runner.py with process group management (SIGTERM -> SIGKILL)
Implement per-task timeout, inactivity timeout / optional heartbeat_pattern, and global timeout
Stream stdout/stderr live, print [N/TOTAL] progress, write test-results/overnight-runner-{timestamp}.log and .json
Implement fail-closed exit codes: 0 all passed, 1 task failure/timeout/stuck, 2 runner/global timeout error
Provide a dry-run script that proves termination for completion, infinite hang, error, global timeout, and stuck/inactivity
Block any command/on_complete string containing shutdown/poweroff/halt/osascript/pmset as a static guard
success_criteria: python3 scripts/overnight_runner.py --dry-run completes within 60s with all expected PASS/TIMEOUT/KILLED/STUCK outcomes
A real batch of sleep/echo commands completes and produces .log + .json summary
A sleep 1000 task with timeout_seconds=5 is KILLED and runner exits 1
A silent task exceeding inactivity_timeout_seconds is marked STUCK and KILLED
A two-task sleep 1000 batch with global_timeout_seconds=10 aborts within 10s
No shutdown/poweroff/halt/osascript/pmset string appears in runner source except in governance comments

kpi_targets.inactivity_detection: STUCK after inactivity_timeout_seconds of no matching output

integration_points: test-results/ directory for logs and summaries
dependencies: No dependency on OPS-SHUTDOWN-003/004/005/006 (registry not used)

invariants: .windsurf/rules/50-shutdown-governance.md — only scripts/shutdownManager/shutdownExecutor.ts may execute macOS shutdown; this runner must only terminate process groups and exit cleanly
.windsurf/rules/00-project-invariants.md — config-first: all timeouts/intervals/read defaults from JSON config, no hardcoded operational values
No new canonical entities (Execution/Attempt/Claim/Lease/Heartbeat) may be introduced
forbidden_actions: Do NOT call shutdown, poweroff, halt, osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to shut down', pmset sleep, sudo shutdown -h now, or any equivalent
Do NOT modify Coordinator, Strategist, ProjectRunner, Execution Runtime, scripts/shutdownManager/**, or scripts/run_with_timeout.py
Do NOT write to localStorage/sessionStorage or use PersistenceService (ops-only file logs)
Do NOT create UI components, .css files, or React Context/Zustand stores

integration_tests: Dry-run with 5 scenarios: complete, infinite hang, error, global timeout, stuck/inactivity

lint.scope: scripts/overnight_runner/ (if Python lint configured, otherwise skip; at minimum grep for forbidden shutdown strings)

notes.process_group: Use subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True). The child PID equals the new PGID. On timeout/inactivity kill the whole group with os.killpg(pgid, SIGTERM), wait grace_period_seconds, then os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL).
notes.inactivity_vs_heartbeat: If heartbeat_pattern is null, any stdout/stderr output resets the inactivity timer. If set, only lines matching the regex reset it.
notes.global_timeout: Track absolute monotonic start time. If a new task would exceed the global deadline, abort before starting it; if the current task exceeds it, kill and exit.
notes.shutdown_guard: Before executing any command or on_complete, reject strings containing shutdown|poweroff|halt|osascript|pmset|tell application.*shut down|sudo shutdown. Log the rejection and exit 2.
notes.handoff: After completion, the coordinator may continue with OPS-SHUTDOWN-003+ for the canonical Global Session Shutdown Manager. This runner is a tactical bridge, not its replacement.
